_about: PolarisAI data config. The build script combines this file with etf_core.db, etf_context.db and etf_prices.db to write etf-data.js. Edit this file to change placeholders, assumptions or rules; rerun the script after every edit.

cas.name: Canadian stocks
cas.about: Follows Canadian companies across the whole market

uss.name: US stocks
uss.about: Follows large US companies across the market

ins.name: International developed-market stocks
ins.ex: Developed countries outside North America, such as Japan, the UK, France, Germany, Switzerland and Australia.
ins.about: Developed countries outside North America, such as Japan, the UK, France, Germany, Switzerland and Australia

ems.name: Emerging-market stocks
ems.ex: Faster-growing developing economies, mainly China, India, Taiwan, South Korea and Brazil. Higher growth potential, bigger ups and downs.
ems.about: Faster-growing developing economies, mainly China, India, Taiwan, South Korea and Brazil. They swing more, so this slice stays small

cab.name: Canadian bonds
cab.about: Canadian government and corporate bonds of all maturities. Bonds add stability when stocks fall

cst.name: Canadian short-term bonds
cst.about: Short-term Canadian government and corporate bonds, which move less when interest rates change

glb.name: Global bonds
glb.about: Government and corporate bonds from around the world, including the US

_rules: Core pick = lowest MER among broad funds in the category that fit the risk level and preferences; ties go to the larger fund (aum_cad_m). US-listed funds are allowed unless the client picks Canadian-dollar ETFs only.

assumptions._about: Expected long-run yearly returns before fees (percent). Volatility and correlation come from the weekly prices; fallback_vol is used only for placeholder funds with no prices.

_placeholders: Step 4 lists are placeholders until the fund database carries the right funds. Values here are used only when a fund is missing from etf_core.db.

ems.name: iShares Core MSCI Emerging Markets IMI Index ETF

cab.name: Mackenzie Canadian Strategic Fixed Income ETF

cst.name: Dynamic Short Term Credit Plus Fund/ETF

glb.name: BMO US Aggregate Bond Index ETF (hedged)

cab.name: Dynamic Short Term Credit Plus Fund/ETF

glb.name: BMO US Aggregate Bond Index ETF (hedged)

themes.label: Inflation-protected bonds
themes.name: iShares Canadian Real Return Bond Index ETF

themes.label: Asia-Pacific
themes.note: Good to know: you already own some Asia-Pacific companies through your international and emerging-market funds. VA adds more of Japan, Australia, South Korea, Hong Kong and Singapore. It swings more than a broad world fund, and its value moves with those currencies.

themes.label: Energy and natural resources
themes.name: iShares S&P/TSX Capped Energy Index ETF

themes.label: Technology (including AI)
themes.name: TD Global Technology Leaders Index ETF
themes.note: Good to know: this fund holds the world’s largest technology companies, including the leaders in artificial intelligence. About half of it is in five companies. It swings more than the overall market.

extras.label: Cryptocurrency (bitcoin)
extras.name: Purpose Bitcoin ETF
extras.warn: Bitcoin can rise or fall by more than half in a year. You could lose most of this slice.

extras.label: Leveraged US stocks (2×)
extras.name: BetaPro S&P 500 2x Daily Bull ETF
extras.warn: This fund aims for twice the daily move of US stocks. Losses are magnified too, and over long periods it can lose value even when the market rises.

schema_requests.ask: Add a hedge_currency column (CAD, USD or none). cad_hedged is currently 1 for any hedged fund, so BNDW and BNDX (hedged to US dollars) look CAD-hedged.
Add a broad_market flag (1 = whole-market index fund). The site currently guesses from fund names to keep single-country, factor and target-maturity funds out of the core picks.

Add theme tags (or an app_theme table) for the eight step 4 themes: inflation-protected bonds, real estate, gold, infrastructure, Asia-Pacific, energy, technology, clean energy. Gold and Asia-Pacific have no tag today.

Decide whether swap and second-fund lists should be generated from the data (next-lowest fees, correlation under 0.95) or stored as a table (app_swap: category, ticker, rank). Either way, every ticker used must be eligible.
Optional: move the expected-return assumptions per category into a table (capital_market_assumptions) so they are versioned with the data.
Optional: add an is_active flag so the site can say whether a fund tracks an index or is actively managed.
